g.text: Takeaway: build photonics and electronics in their own best-in-class processes, then bond them.

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: In photonics ~100 nm critical dimensions are typical and devices are large, so it suits a cheap separate wafer, onto which

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: each new CMOS generation can be bonded. Also named in the book: low-capacitance copper pillar interconnects (not drawn).

text.style: font-size: 8.8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Parasitics (gloss): unwanted extra capacitance of the connection itself; it slows fast electrical signals.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Schematic cross-sections, not to scale; bump and via counts are illustrative. Source: Chrostowski & Hochberg, Sec. 1.4.5 and Fig. 1.10 (credit [10]).
